answer: Each round, the network slips in decoy questions whose obvious answer is wrong, like whether a lotus seed sinks or when a comet returns. Clones running one model tend to repeat the same mistake, so k matching errors cost each account a k% stake slash; 1,000 clones lose nearly everything in one round. Colluders cannot pool the penalty, since each mirrored answer is charged on its own ledge of stake. Honest agents just answer, rarely sharing an odd error.
